content.text:
Below are quick illustrative results (use your calculator with your exact inputs for accurate numbers). *These are sample scenarios to show how outputs look.*

Sample: ₹10,00,000 BSA (Basic Sum Assured)
  • Age 30, PPT 12 → Est. annual premium ≈ ₹95,000 → Survival Income (after PPT) ≈ 8% of BSA = ₹80,000/yr (paid annually for life) + Guaranteed Additions during PPT.
  • Age 40, PPT 8 → Est. annual premium ≈ ₹1,10,000 → Survival Income ≈ ₹80,000/yr.
(Numbers are illustrative — actual premium depends on LIC tables, medical underwriting and riders.)

Jeevan Umang is a participating whole-life plan that provides an ongoing (lifelong) survival income after the premium paying term. It combines life insurance protection with a recurring income stream — making it attractive for retirement planning. The plan also accrues bonuses and may include final additional bonuses where applicable.

sections.title: How the LIC Jeevan Umang calculator works (formulas explained)

content.heading: Premium calculation
content.body:
• Base annual premium = lookup from LIC rate table depending on Age, BSA and PPT.
  • Mode conversion (to monthly/quarterly/half-yearly) uses modal loading factors:
    • Yearly × 1.00 = Yearly
    • Half-yearly = Yearly × 0.5098
    • Quarterly = Yearly × 0.2575
    • Monthly = Yearly × 0.0879
    (Your calculator should compute and display all four modes when you enter a yearly premium.)

content.heading: Guaranteed Additions (GAs)
content.body:
• GAs are paid during the Premium Paying Term at a fixed rate per ₹1,000 of BSA (displayed by the plan).
  • Total GAs = Annual GA × PPT.

content.heading: Survival income (post-PPT)
content.body:
• Regular income is typically expressed as a percentage of BSA paid annually after PPT (e.g., many LIC whole-life income plans pay ~8% of BSA as yearly income; verify current brochure rate).
  • Flexi / accumulate options: if offered, unwithdrawn income may accumulate at a guaranteed rate.

content.heading: Maturity & death benefits
content.body:
• For whole-life income plans, the main benefit is the lifetime income; death benefit typically equals Sum Assured on Death (as per brochure) or guaranteed minimum (e.g., 105% of total premiums paid). Check the plan UIN for exact terms.

Accuracy note: Where the plan uses declared bonuses or special additions, the calculator uses illustrative/default values but always shows a clear disclaimer and 'last updated' date.

sections.title: Inputs explained (what each field means and why it matters)

content.heading: Age / gender
content.body: Younger entrants pay lower premiums; gender may affect premium in some tables (if allowed by the insurer/regulator).

content.heading: Basic Sum Assured (BSA)
content.body: This is the core coverage amount — both survival income and Guaranteed Additions are derived from BSA.

content.heading: Premium Paying Term (PPT)
content.body: Shorter PPT = higher annual premium but faster income start or lower total premium years. Typical PPT options include several discrete choices (e.g., 10, 12, 15 years) — use the preset list.

content.heading: Payment Mode
content.body: Yearly is cheapest (lowest modal loading). Monthly is convenient but slightly costlier due to modal loading.

content.heading: Riders
content.body: Optional covers (Accidental Death & Disability, Critical Illness) add separate premium lines and do not normally change GA or survival income but do increase the payable premium.

content.text: *These examples are illustrative — use the calculator for exact figures.

content.heading: Example 1 — Young saver (age 30, BSA ₹10L, PPT 12)
content.body:
• Input: Age 30, BSA 10,00,000, PPT 12, Yearly mode
  • Calculator outputs:
    • Annual premium ≈ ₹95,000
    • GAs during PPT (e.g., ₹X per ₹1,000 × 12 yrs) → total GAs ≈ ₹Y
    • Post-PPT survival income = 8% × BSA = ₹80,000/yr (paid for life)
    • Estimated IRR ~5–6% (tax-free component considered)

content.heading: Example 2 — Pre-retiree (age 50, BSA ₹15L, PPT 8)
content.body:
• Input: Age 50, BSA 15,00,000, PPT 8
  • Outputs:
    • Annual premium ≈ ₹2,15,000
    • Guaranteed Additions accumulate during 8 yrs
    • Survival income post-PPT = ₹1,20,000/yr (10% of BSA would be ₹1.5L — confirm plan %)

content.heading: Example 3 — High SA (age 35, BSA ₹1 Cr, PPT 10)
content.body: Illustrates high sum assured rebate logic (LIC often provides rebates at higher SA bands) — calculator applies high SA rebate automatically when applicable.

sections.title: Surrender, paid-up & loans — what the calculator shows

items: Paid-up value: If premiums stop after 2+ years, policy becomes paid-up. Paid-up SA reduces proportionately to premiums paid; calculator can simulate paid-up outcomes.

Surrender value: Available after the policy acquires surrender value (usually after 2 yrs). Calculator estimates Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV) or Special Surrender Value (SSV) based on paid premiums and vested benefits.
Loan: You can take a loan against the policy up to a percentage of SSV — calculator shows an estimated loan amount and interest impact.

sections.title: Practical tips to reduce premium or improve value

items: Pick a longer PPT (if you can afford the time) — reduces annual premium.
Avoid unnecessary riders — only add riders you truly need.
Start earlier — age is the single biggest determinant of premium.
Check high SA rebates — if you’re going for large sums assured, you may get a discount.

items.q: 1. What is the Jeevan Umang calculator and is it free?
items.a: The Jeevan Umang calculator is a free online tool to estimate premiums, survival income and related values for LIC Plan 745. It provides quick, illustrative figures — not a binding LIC quote.

items.q: 2. How do I calculate Jeevan Umang premium?
items.a: Enter your age, BSA, PPT and mode into the calculator. The tool uses LIC rate tables (or illustrative assumptions) and modal factors to compute yearly and mode premiums.

items.q: 3. What is the survival income under Jeevan Umang?
items.a: Survival income is a yearly payment after PPT — typically a fixed percentage of Basic Sum Assured (the specific percent is defined in the plan brochure). The calculator displays this as an annual amount.

items.q: 4. Does the calculator include riders and GST?
items.a: Yes — toggle riders to see additional rider premiums. The calculator also shows GST (first year/renewal rates) in the premium breakdown.
Results are estimates. For a binding quote and acceptance, contact LIC or an authorized agent. The calculator is accurate to the extent of the input assumptions (bonus, FAB, rebate rates).

items.q: 6. Can NRIs use the Jeevan Umang calculator?
items.a: Yes, NRIs can use the calculator for planning, but actual purchase and eligibility depend on LIC and FEMA rules.

items.q: 7. When can I take a loan against Jeevan Umang?
items.a: Loans are typically available after the policy acquires a surrender value (commonly after 2 full years). The calculator estimates the loanable amount based on SSV.
Generally, policy payouts under life insurance may be tax-favored under Section 10(10D), but tax laws change — consult a tax advisor.
If premiums stop after at least two full years, your policy becomes paid-up. The calculator can show the reduced paid-up SA and expected maturity/paid-up benefits.

items.q: 10. How to compare Jeevan Umang with Jeevan Utsav or Jeevan Labh?
items.a: Use the side-by-side comparison feature: input identical BSA and check income vs maturity outcomes to choose the best fit for your goals.
